# montecarlo_ingestion_key (Resource)

An ingestion key is a key id and secret that pushes metadata, lineage, query logs, ETL jobs and runs, or BI assets to the one warehouse or container it is scoped to. The secret is returned only when the key is created. A warehouse or container can hold several keys, so create the new one before deleting the old one when rotating.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `bi_container_id` (String) The BI container to push BI assets to, such as a `custom-bi-connector` container. Send exactly one of this, `warehouse_id` and `etl_container_id`.
- `description` (String) What this key is for. Monte Carlo generates one naming the warehouse or container if you leave it out.
- `etl_container_id` (String) The ETL container to push ETL jobs and runs to, such as a `custom-etl-connector` container. Send exactly one of this, `warehouse_id` and `bi_container_id`.
- `warehouse_id` (String) The warehouse to push metadata, lineage and query logs to. Send exactly one of this, `bi_container_id` and `etl_container_id`.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) When the key was created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the key.
- `mcd_id` (String) Key id to present, as the `x-mcd-id` header or a client's `mcd_id` setting. The same value as `id`.
- `mcd_token` (String, Sensitive) Secret to present, as the `x-mcd-token` header or a client's `mcd_token` setting. Returned once, by this call, and not retrievable afterwards. Terraform keeps it in state, so anyone who can read the state can read the secret: `sensitive` only hides it from CLI output. Keep state in a backend that encrypts it and limits who can read it. Hand the secret on through a write-only argument, such as `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string_wo`, not through an output, because a `sensitive` output is stored in state too. To rotate, create a new key and delete this one.
